metric.installation_distribution_experie.observation_window: current state of quidra-lang/quidra default branch docs and public release history as of snapshot date
metric.installation_distribution_experie.rubric: 0-100 proxy applied identically to all languages: points for (a) an official one-line/scripted installer, (b) presence in at least one mainstream OS/language package manager (apt/brew/choco/winget/scoop/etc.), (c) official prebuilt multi-platform binary artifacts attached to releases, (d) a single-binary or low-dependency install, (e) containerized (Docker) distribution, (f) version-manager integration, (g) clarity/completeness of documented install steps. Score is the weighted proportion of these signals actually observed as of the snapshot date.
metric.installation_distribution_experie.score_rationale: Positive signals: automated, CI-gated multi-asset GitHub Releases for every tagged version; a deliberately safety-hardened library package installer (exact-tag resolution, manifest/hash verification, sandboxed asset extraction) documented in packages.md; clear, reproducible source-build instructions. Negative signals: no first-party OS/language package-manager listing found (apt/brew/choco/winget/scoop), no curl-pipe-bash installer, no Docker image, no version-manager plugin, and building from source requires several native library dev headers (libcurl, libpng, libjpeg, libtiff, libwebp) plus a pre-existing Clang 15+ install because the project intentionally does not bundle a backend toolchain. Net effect: a functional but source-build-centric, single-ecosystem (GitHub Releases + git-based library installer) distribution experience, well below languages with broad package-manager and one-line-installer coverage.

sources.finding: Release workflow on push to main creates the GitHub Release and all supported platform artifacts; release is not complete while that workflow is failing or incomplete.

quidra install resolves only exact vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH release tags via git, optionally downloading HTTPS platform assets (asset.<platform>) that are inspected before extraction; asset-backed installs additionally require curl and tar, and official Linux packages declare those runtime dependencies. This is the package manager for Quidra *libraries* (dnn, vision), not for installing the Quidra compiler/toolchain itself.

Building the compiler documents CMake + Clang 15+ plus libcurl/libpng/libjpeg/libtiff/libwebp development headers as prerequisites, and states the distribution intentionally does not bundle a backend toolchain (Clang must already be installed); the documented path is cmake -S . -B build && cmake --build build && ctest && ./build/quidra run examples/hello.qui, i.e. source build.

Tagged releases v0.1.0, v0.2.0, v0.3.0, v0.3.1 each carry attached release assets (6, 6, 6, and 4 assets respectively), consistent with automated per-platform artifact publication, but no evidence was found of listing in any OS or language package manager (apt, Homebrew, Chocolatey, winget, scoop), no install-script (curl|bash) entry point, and no Docker image or version-manager (asdf/mise-style) integration.

The hosted browser playground explicitly carries no compiler and instructs: to actually run a program, install Quidra and use quidra run, confirming there is no zero-install hosted execution path for the toolchain itself.

metric.toolchain_stability_release_matur.observation_window: public release history and embedded development.md workflow as of snapshot date
metric.toolchain_stability_release_matur.rubric: 0-100 proxy applied identically to all languages, scoring only frozen currently observable evidence: (a) whether releases are reproducible/immutable and tag-verified, (b) documented versioning/support policy (SemVer or equivalent) and its actual observance, (c) compatibility guarantees, including whether format/ABI-level contracts are versioned independently of the product version, (d) supported-artifact availability at each release, (e) maintenance/release cadence including patch releases, (f) documented stability commitments and CI gating rigor before a release is cut. Language age/first-release date are recorded as metadata only and are not scored.
metric.toolchain_stability_release_matur.score_rationale: Positive signals: a genuinely mechanized, reproducible, single-source-of-truth release pipeline (project.toml -> sync_metadata.py -> CI-gated, immutable, bot-created tags) with independently versioned ABI/IR/schema compatibility numbers, a documented and enforced SemVer policy, an unusually rigorous pre-release CI/test checklist, verified (GPG-signed) release commits, and real observed history including a patch-level maintenance release (v0.3.1). Negative signals: the language is still pre-1.0, so by its own documented policy 0.X.0 releases may include breaking language/stdlib changes and there is no published LTS/backport support-window commitment beyond 'fix release blockers on develop'; the released history is short (four tags across about four days) so long-run cadence and support-policy durability are not yet demonstrated. Net effect: process/reproducibility maturity is high, but compatibility-guarantee strength is still that of an actively evolving pre-1.0 product, yielding a moderate score.

sources.finding: Quidra uses Semantic Versioning with a documented, mechanically enforced release procedure: version is set once in project.toml (single source of truth), python3 scripts/sync_metadata.py regenerates all derived metadata and metadata_ssot_tests.py fails the build on any drift; a release tag vX.Y.Z is immutable, is never created or pushed by hand, and the release workflow itself refuses to continue if that tag already exists.

A release requires green CI including GCC and Clang release builds, Linux/macOS/Windows CI, sanitizer and warnings-as-errors builds, ctest, parser/checker negative tests, native runtime smoke tests, standard-library/module tests, package/version/lockfile tests, REPL/CLI tests, packaging tests, and documented-example checks before promotion to main.

The device ABI, typed Quidra IR, package-manifest schema, and package lockfile schema each carry their own version number declared in project.toml, deliberately independent of the compiler/product version, so a later release can raise one without raising the others; package import enforces exact ABI-version equality as a hard compatibility gate (PACKAGE_COMPATIBILITY).

Four tags exist to date (v0.1.0, v0.2.0, v0.3.0, v0.3.1), each created by the github-actions bot rather than a human, with v0.3.0->v0.3.1 showing an actual maintenance/patch release; PR #3 promoting v0.2.0 records that the develop HEAD passed the full CI matrix (GCC/Clang, sanitizers, macOS, Windows, packaging, and dtype coverage) before merge to main, and at least one release commit (v0.2.0) carries a GitHub-verified GPG signature.

sources.finding: Quidra never installs or releases from a moving branch: package/version resolution enumerates only exact vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH tags, and first-party libraries (dnn, vision) are documented as being re-pinned and re-released against an already-tagged core release rather than an unreleased develop/feature state.
